subject: Post-call: Request log sampling & redaction scope (CureWell)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@curewell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Request log sampling & redaction scope (CureWell)

Hi Danielle — thanks again for the call earlier. Recapping next steps on logging controls so we have a shared scope to validate with your security/procurement teams.

Key points we agreed on during the demo:
- CureWell needs request/response telemetry for troubleshooting and performance analytics, but PII must be removed before any long-term storage.
- Short-term, we can keep an unredacted, encrypted ring buffer for 48 hours for incident debug (access via audited role-based access).
- Long-term logs stored in Redwood's observability pipeline must have PII redacted or tokenized; headers with identifiers require scrubbing or deterministic hashing.
- Data residency: production logs for CureWell in US-only region (AWS us-east-1) per contract baseline.

Proposed approach (for your review):
1) Sampling: adaptive sampling at 5% for production traffic, with session-prioritized sampling (higher probability for requests that result in errors or elevated latency). We also proposed a manual sampling override for support sessions.
2) PII detection & redaction: run a two-stage filter — first pass pattern-based redaction (SSNs, credit card patterns, emails) followed by ML-based PII classifier for names/addresses. Redacted values replaced with token placeholders like [PII_REDACTED:HASH].
3) Trace identifiers: do not store raw trace IDs in long-term logs. Store a salted deterministic hash to permit cross-log correlation while preventing retrieval of original trace IDs.
4) Headers & cookies: drop or mask any headers marked as "sensitive" by CureWell (your list). We'll provide a header scrubbing config file you can edit in the Console.
5) Retention windows: 48h unredacted ring buffer (encrypted), 90 days redacted logs for analytics, 365 days aggregated metrics only (no request payloads).

Deliverables we'll send by EOD Monday:
- A short proposal (PDF) with the above scope and SLAs.
- A sampling matrix (spreadsheet) showing how adaptive sampling scales with traffic and error rates.
- A redaction ruleset dump (text) with our default patterns and ML classifier thresholds.

Please confirm if the above aligns with what you expect. Two quick questions for your security/procurement folks so we can align the contract:
- Is 48 hours of unredacted debug buffer acceptable under your SOC2/PCI policies?
- Do you have any specific hashing salt management requirements (customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed)?

Thanks — tagging Ben & Marissa for any implementation notes they want to add.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Request log sampling & redaction scope (CureWell)

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from security/procurement side before we proceed: 

1) 48h unredacted buffer: acceptable for engineering/debugging only if access is logged and tied to an approved incident ticket. We will need proof of audit logs during the pilot.
2) Hashing salt: we prefer customer-managed KMS for anything that could enable re-identification. Can Redwood support a customer KMS key in us-east-1?
3) Sampling: we like session-prioritized sampling, but we'd like an initial pilot at 2% before scaling to 5% post-acceptance to keep costs conservative.

Also, procurement asked whether any full request payloads will be included in the 90-day redacted logs (we want only non-sensitive fields and metadata).

I'll share this with procurement and security; copying procurement inbox for their internal checklist.

—Danielle
Danielle Ortiz
VP Product Operations | CureWell Health Systems
danielle.ortiz@curewell.com

Thanks for the quick feedback, Danielle — answers inline below.

1) Access & audit logs: agreed. We will include per-request access logs for the ring buffer with user, role, timestamp, and ticket id. We'll export a sample audit trail for procurement during the pilot.

2) Customer-managed KMS: yes, Redwood supports trusting a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) in AWS KMS. We can configure the ring buffer and object storage encryption to use your CMK in us-east-1. I'll add that as a required line in the MA proposal.

3) Sampling pilot: happy to start at 2% for the pilot (30 days). After pilot acceptance, we can raise to 5% and enable error-prioritized sampling. We'll include the sampling matrix in the Drive link.

Regarding the 90-day redacted logs: Redwood will store request/response metadata, headers (after scrubbing), and non-sensitive fields. Full request payloads will be excluded unless they've been redacted/tokenized by the pipeline. We'll add explicit examples in the proposal showing what is kept vs removed.

Attached: CureWell_MAProposal_v1.pdf (proposal) — includes a dedicated appendix on redaction rules and KMS notes. Also attaching cw_sampling_matrix_v1.xlsx.

Next actions (I propose):
- Procurement: confirm CMK onboarding timeline (procurement@curewell.com).
- Security: review the redaction ruleset and confirm whether the ML thresholds are acceptable (we will provide a test dataset).
- Redwood: send a signed pilot addendum for 30-day 2% sampling and CMK config.

If that looks good, Ben can take the technical onboarding and run the pilot checklist.

Best,
Naomi

Quick operational notes from my side — flagged items we need to action for the pilot: 
- Pilot config: enable adaptive sampler with these tiers: 2% baseline, 10x weight for errored requests, 5x weight for new-session flags. I attached cw_sampling_matrix_v1.xlsx.
- PII detector: we'll add a custom rule for your patient-id format (CW-<6 digits>) — will require a sample file from security.
- Trace ID policy: implement deterministic HMAC-SHA256 hashing with a per-customer salt (stored in your CMK via envelope encryption). This gives correlation but prevents raw ID exposure.
- Audit evidence: exportable audit-log bundle for any ring-buffer access; I recommend quarterly access reviews.

I'll draft the pilot checklist and drop it in the Drive link. Naomi — I can own the pilot runbook and the initial infra config if you want me to coordinate with CureWell's security contact.

—Ben
